facts.claim: 1931년 영국 신문 The Times 용으로 의뢰된 세리프 서체
facts.note: Times New Roman is a serif typeface commissioned for use by the British newspaper The Times in 1931.

facts.claim: 모노타입 미술 자문 모리슨이 기획, 광고부 레터링 화가 라든트와 협업
facts.note: The typeface was conceived by Stanley Morison, the artistic adviser to the British branch of the printing equipment company Monotype, in collaboration with Victor Lardent, a lettering artist in The Times's advertising department.
Morison proposed an older Monotype typeface named Plantin as a basis for the design ... The main change was that the contrast between strokes was enhanced to give a crisper image.
The new design made its debut in The Times on 3 October 1932.

facts.claim: 40년 원래 서체, 1972~2007 다섯 번 변형판 교체
facts.note: The Times stayed with the original Times New Roman for 40 years. The paper subsequently switched between different variants of the original typeface five times between 1972 and 2007
